real_sample.derived_from: corpus/worlds/Paper/level.dat (real, local-only, hash recorded in corpus/worlds/manifest.json; a real current-PaperMC server world Cameron generated live 2026-08-13, DataVersion 4903)
real_sample.sanitization: Same re-serialization approach as java-real-legacy-fields-full-extraction-succeeds's sample: only the inspected Data-compound keys are kept (GameType, DataVersion, Time, LevelName, difficulty_settings), LevelName replaced by a placeholder. Critically, this sample's absence of legacy Data.Difficulty and Data.WorldGenSettings/Data.RandomSeed is itself real -- the original level.dat genuinely does not contain those keys (confirmed by parsing the real file directly before sanitizing), not an artifact of the reduction.

notes: Real, current MSC 1 evidence (server 'paper', current-PaperMC, DataVersion 4903 -- newer than campack's 3465) where the legacy fields extractSeedString and extractDifficultyString look for genuinely do not exist: this server stores difficulty as a string under Data.difficulty_settings.difficulty ('normal') instead of the legacy Data.Difficulty integer tag, and stores no world seed under Data at all (no RandomSeed, no WorldGenSettings). MSC 1's WorldSlotManager.swift never reads difficulty_settings or any string-typed difficulty/seed representation -- extractDifficultyString and extractSeedString only look for integer tags at their known paths, so both genuinely return nil against this real, current server, not a synthetic worst case. extractDayTime falls through its Java-preferred Data.DayTime path (absent here) to Data.Time (present, 20927) -- the real file exercises that exact fallback. This is a real gap Phase 6's port inherits as-is per oracle fidelity (D-... none override this), worth flagging to Cameron since it means MSC 2 will also show 'seed unknown' for modern Paper worlds until a follow-up decision adds the string-based paths -- noted in this step's questions rather than fixed here.
